documents.title: Frontier Agreement between Afghanistan and the USSR, with Protocol and exchange of notes
documents.publicationCitation: United Nations Treaty Series, vol. 31, No. 476, pp. 147–168.
documents.notes: Signed 13 June 1946; UNTS footnote records entry into force on 17 January 1947 by exchange of ratifications at Kabul. Article 1 establishes thalweg/principal-fairway/median rules on the Amu-Darya and Pyandzh and preserves Aral-Pagambar for the USSR and Urta-Tagai for Afghanistan. Article 2 requires a Mixed Commission to map Khamiab–Lake Sar-i-Kul, determine islands, establish posts where necessary, and produce a detailed description and map for government ratification. The Protocol terminates Articles 9 and 10 of the 1921 RSFSR-Afghanistan treaty. The exchange of notes requires Zulfikar–Khamiab re-demarcation from the 1885–1888 Anglo-Russian documents and maps.

documents.title: Treaty concerning the regime of the Soviet-Afghan State frontier
documents.publicationCitation: United Nations Treaty Series, vol. 321, No. 4655, pp. 165 ff.
documents.notes: Article 1 authoritatively identifies the Zulfikar–Zor-Kul line as determined by the 1946 Agreement plus demarcation and re-demarcation documents dated 29 September 1948; the re-demarcation documents were drafted on the basis of the 1885–1888 protocol. It separately states that Zor-Kul–China is determined by the 1895 demarcation protocols. UNTS records entry into force on 5 October 1958.
